mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in each of the last four weeks with accelerating magnitude (-25.7, -31.9, -44.1, -59.9). This monotonic, steepening decline reflects a self-reinforcing activity-suppression trend (closures, reduced discretionary trips) that is likely to persist, pushing the next-28-day mean further below the last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined every week for 4 consecutive weeks with increasing weekly magnitude
failure_condition: If the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than the last 28-day mean despite the observed accelerating 4-week decline, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen from 8.7 to 19.4 percent over four weeks, indicating stay-home compliance with tightening policy measures. Once RESIDENTIAL exceeds a 15-point sustained threshold, it signals binding stay-at-home orders that mechanically suppress non-essential retail trips for the following weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean exceeds 15 percentage points above baseline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 15.9 and 19.4 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 2-4 weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 15 points, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-60.7) and WORKPLACES (-37.7) have collapsed together over the last four weeks. Commute-linked incidental retail trips (lunch stops, after-work shopping) depend on both mobility channels being active; their joint collapse removes a behavioral pathway to retail visits beyond what either series alone would predict, amplifying the RETAIL_REC decline.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -33.6 to -60.7 and WORKPLACES fell from -20.9 to -37.7 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC decline over the next 4 weeks is no larger than predicted by TRANSIT or WORKPLACES declines individually (i.e., no amplification detected), the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under a red-zone lockdown regime, a sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility (from +0.1 to -32.4 points, a 32.5-point collapse) signals that outdoor movement restrictions have newly bound, which typically coincides with closures or capacity limits on retail and recreation venues, driving further RETAIL_REC decline in the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 25 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from 0.1 to -18.4 to -32.4 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not fall further in the week immediately following a PARKS drop exceeding 25 points, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Late November marks the onset of pre-Christmas shopping demand in Italy (e.g., Black Friday and holiday gift purchasing). Even under restrictive conditions, essential and click-and-collect retail activity tends to partially rebound seasonally, causing RETAIL_REC to decelerate its decline or modestly recover over the next four weeks relative to the prior trend.
candidate_trigger: calendar period falls within the 4 weeks surrounding late-November holiday shopping onset
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2020-11-15 is within the pre-holiday shopping season
regime_hint: holiday run-up season under tightening restrictions
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline at the same or faster rate through the holiday period with no deceleration or rebound, the seasonal mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility is a leading indicator of retail footfall because reduced transit use directly limits physical access to retail and recreation destinations. TRANSIT's steep week-on-week fall (from -53.0 to -60.7) precedes and predicts a continued fall in RETAIL_REC in the immediate following week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell every week for 4 consecutive weeks reaching -60.7
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a continued TRANSIT drop, the leading-indicator mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has declined much less steeply (-9.1 to -23.4) than RETAIL_REC (-25.7 to -59.9), indicating a substitution effect where consumers concentrate trips into essential grocery/pharmacy visits while abandoning discretionary retail. Once the gap between RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM declines exceeds 30 points, this substitution pattern is expected to persist and widen further.
candidate_trigger: gap between RETAIL_REC decline and GROCERY_PHARM decline exceeds 30 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:gap between the two series widened from 16.6 to 36.5 points over 4 weeks
failure_condition: If the gap between RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM narrows over the next 2 weeks instead of widening, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous deterioration in WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and rise in RESIDENTIAL reflects a coordinated lockdown-policy regime where mobility channels reinforce each other: reduced commuting (WORKPLACES, TRANSIT) combined with increased home confinement (RESIDENTIAL) compounds to suppress RETAIL_REC more than any single channel would, over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series moved in a mutually reinforcing direction over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC decline over the next 4 weeks is no greater than what WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, or RESIDENTIAL individually would predict via simple additive extrapolation, the interaction/compounding mechanism is rejected.
